🚨SHOCKING | Mystery waves in a well for several days raises concern; here’s the REAL REASON behind it;

👇🏼: Read more

An 18-foot-deep well in Virparda village of Gujarat’s Morbi district has begun generating continuous waves and ripples, drawing large crowds and raising concerns among locals.

This is not a mystery, but the phenomena is known as Well Seiche, a standing-wave oscillation of water inside an open well that produces continuous ripples, waves, or sloshing

“When I arrived at my farm, water from the well was spilling over the edge. It has continued like this ever since,” said the owner, Pranjivan Sadariya, who first noticed the unusual activity on August 2.

Villagers, passersby and travellers along a nearby highway have been gathering in large numbers over the past five days to witness the strange movement of water.

The phenomenon has triggered curiosity as well as fears of possible seismic activity, but officials have ruled out any such link.

“This is not seismic activity. Prima facie, it appears that following heavy upstream rainfall, groundwater is recharging and air trapped in the pore spaces of rocks is being released, causing the disturbance in the well,” said District Geologist J S Vadher.

He added that the Institute of Seismological Research in Gandhinagar has confirmed there is no active fault line in the area.

The most likely cause is hydrological pressure change from rapid groundwater recharge, combined with the release of trapped air.

The “mysterious” moving water is a natural, temporary response of the aquifer to heavy rain - air and pressure pulses exciting the well’s natural resonance. Once recharge stabilises and the trapped air is fully released, the oscillations stop.
